key_insight: DemoFoundry combines coding agents, physics simulation, and generative rendering to produce photorealistic robot demonstrations with aligned states and action labels.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a path to scaling robot-training data without target-task human demonstrations or detailed scene appearance modeling.
method: Coding agents build aligned real–proxy video pairs to train a video renderer.
Given a scene reference and task instruction, agents reconstruct task-relevant geometry and write executable robot-control programs.
Physics simulation generates trajectories; automated checks select successful executions for photorealistic rendering and policy learning.
evidence_signal: Experiments report improved visual quality and action–video consistency, with generated-data policies outperforming raw-simulation training and approaching training on an equal number of real demonstrations.
watch_item: Deployment should verify that generative rendering preserves task-critical contacts and geometry; the abstract provides no quantitative results or evaluation scope.
paper_title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
